patch_description: The best prior program (score 0.59) used a constant-velocity Kalman prefilter followed by a single fixed zero-phase Savitzky-Golay (SG) pass. The feedback identifies the smoothness/responsiveness tradeoff as the active frontier: a fixed SG half-window is either too wide (lag, damped turns) or too narrow (residual ripple that still triggers false reversals). The signal is non-stationary, so noise level varies strongly across the record. I replace the current constant-acceleration Kalman + RTS smoother (0.56, which regressed vs. 0.59) with the winning architecture and make the SG half-window *locally adaptive* using the local-volatility array (`local_std`) already computed in Stage 1. For each of three half-window scales (h/2, h, 3h/2) I precompute an order-2 SG kernel and smooth the Kalman output with all three via one convolution each (all O(n), preserving efficiency_score 1.00). Per-sample weights are soft Gaussians in volatility space centered at the 20th/50th/80th percentiles of local volatility, normalized across scales. Volatile regions thus get the wide window (where spurious slope reversals and false reversals originate), quiet regions get the narrow window (preserving the 0.74–0.77 responsiveness and genuine trend dynamics). Soft weighting avoids seams/discontinuities that hard block switching would introduce. Zero-phase convolution keeps lag error low; order-2 polynomials preserve genuine turning points exactly.
